answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether composing a sonnet or appraising a relic. A public beacon marks each enrollment window, and the contract holds every bond through its full term, even if the identity leaves early. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up 1,000 bonds: aliases remain cheap, but gaining marketplace access costs capital and a month of liquidity.
